summary: Episode Six brings therapist and Yoshi Didn't co-host Lilit Arvahi into the recurring David Choe, Asa Akira, Yoshi Obayashi, and Bobby Namba room. It opens with language, migration, habit, and David's argument that adaptation is necessary, then uses Yoshi's supposedly clean UCLA performance to examine artistic repetition and whether a comic can distinguish a durable act from stagnation. The center of the episode shifts into a personality-test session: the participants debate labels, self-reporting, narcissism, sociopathy, empathy, intimacy, work, sacrifice, and whether therapy can separate a useful pattern from a verdict. The longest late section focuses on Yoshi's grievance against a former employer who contacts him while seriously ill; forgiveness, apology, hate, depression, and sadism become concrete rather than hypothetical before psychology trivia ends the formal show.

connections.label: Repetition can be signature or stagnation
connections.note: David still laughs at Yoshi's familiar material and also treats its persistence across years and recordings as evidence that the act is not developing. The archive should make recurrence visible without deciding that repetition has only one meaning.

connections.label: A test score is not a diagnosis
connections.note: Lilit repeatedly distinguishes a narrow self-report instrument from clinical assessment. The group's competitive framing—who is most damaged—conflicts with her attempt to use patterns as openings for inquiry rather than rankings.

connections.label: Adaptation and tradition coexist in Yoshi's migration story
connections.note: Yoshi describes arriving without a shared language at home or school, learning incompatible social rules, and later using travel as permission to act outside familiar expectations. His rigid habits and geographic experimentation are not opposites.

connections.label: Work becomes a defense against pity
connections.note: Asa and David connect sacrifice, self-authorship, and professional community to their limited patience for explanations of failure. The episode exposes both the agency in that position and its risk of erasing unequal constraints.

connections.label: Hate is treated as fuel and symptom
connections.note: Yoshi describes hate as keeping him alive after job loss, while others connect it to depression, grievance, and sadism. The former employer's illness tests whether the emotion protects dignity or prevents any form of repair.

connections.label: Apology is the missing condition
connections.note: Yoshi and Bobby both resist forgiveness when the former employer seeks contact without clearly admitting wrongdoing. Their answers differ from simple cruelty: the requested meeting, serious illness, apology, and accountability are treated as separate facts.
